# Synthetic local-first presentation pipeline
A hypothetical systems design for evidence-preserving technical talks. SYNTHETIC / HYPOTHETICAL TEST MATERIAL. S01 · E_SYN_01.

# Design the pipeline around evidence
Problem: tools draft and arrange slides, while scientific review needs exact data mapping, source lineage, and explicit uncertainty. Test: can independent render backends produce the same editable talk without changing evidence meaning? S02 · E_SYN_01.

# Separate evidence from presentation layout
Source files → evidence ledger → storyboard + figures → backend adapter → PPTX / PDF / HTML. Keep source manifest and QA beside rendered output. S03 · E_SYN_01.

# Keep figures deterministic
Synthetic fixture values (not results): load tier A 120 req/s; tier B 240 req/s; tier C 360 req/s. Preserve each value and unit exactly. S04 · E_SYN_01.

# Layout intent should survive backend changes
Assertion: one claim per slide. Evidence: show source and data. Review: keep caveats visible. Synthetic design example only. S05 · E_SYN_01.

# Track limitations as structured output
Unsupported chart → warning; raster-only element → editability report; missing source ID → build error; unverified evidence → pending state; provider call → opt-in and cost boundary. S06 · E_SYN_01.

# Compare capabilities, not marketing labels
Check export via local command; inspect text, shapes and charts; visually review every page; preserve source IDs in sidecar; record version, dependencies and services. S07 · E_SYN_01.

# A backend is useful only when its boundary is clear
Local renderer: repeatable exports without model calls. AI service: optional drafting with provider and cost disclosed. Scientific QA: outside renderer, checking every output. S08 · E_SYN_01.

# Recommendation for this test
Keep evidence ledger and chart data in a backend-neutral contract. Use mature renderers through isolated adapters; promote one only after same-input, editable-object, and visual checks pass. This synthetic fixture establishes no research performance. S09 · E_SYN_01.
